title: Amazon Q Developer Flaw Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code via MCP Configs
summary: A high-severity flaw in Amazon Q Developer let a malicious repository run commands and steal a developer's cloud credentials. The path was short: a developer opens the repo, trusts the workspace, and Amazon Q does the rest. Amazon has patched it.

sections.technical:
Tracked as CVE-2026-12957 (CVSS 8.5), the bug sat in how Amazon's AI coding assistant handled Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. A high-severity flaw in Amazon Q Developer let a malicious repository run commands and steal a developer's cloud credentials.

title: New Linux pedit COW Exploit Enables Root Access by Poisoning Cached Binaries
summary: A flaw in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem can let a local unprivileged user gain root on affected systems.
card_summary: A flaw in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem can let a local unprivileged user gain root on affected systems.

sections.mitigation: CVE-2026-46331, nicknamed "pedit COW," is an out-of-bounds write in the packet-editing action (act_pedit) that corrupts shared page-cache memory.

email_summary: A flaw in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem can let a local unprivileged user gain root on affected systems. Tracked as CVE-2026-46331.

title: New DirtyClone Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Local Users Gain Root via Cloned Packets
summary: DirtyClone is a new Linux kernel privilege escalation in the DirtyFrag family. JFrog Security Research published a working exploit walkthrough for the flaw on June 25, the first public demonstration for this variant.
card_summary: DirtyClone is a new Linux kernel privilege escalation in the DirtyFrag family. JFrog Security Research published a working exploit walkthrough for the flaw on June 25, the first public demonstration for this variant.

Assessed severity: HIGH. CVSS score: 8.8/10.
